title: Dormant-account "reactivation fee" and OTP vs. free reactivation with KYC at a branch
summary: A caller from Kaveri Bank tells the recipient that their old savings account has become inoperative because it has not been used for over two years. In the fraud case, the caller says it can be reactivated on the phone if the recipient pays a reactivation fee to a UPI ID and then reads out an OTP. In the legitimate case, the caller says the account can be reactivated free of charge by submitting fresh KYC at any branch or through video KYC. The caller asks for nothing on the call and says the bank will confirm reactivation by SMS.

shared_setting.pretext: the account has had no customer transactions for over two years and holds a balance of about [AMOUNT_1] (₹2,000–₹1,50,000).
shared_setting.recipient_profile: an adult who opened the account years ago (for example for a former job) and now banks elsewhere; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Both callers say the balance is safe but cannot be used until the account is reactivated.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller demands a payment to a caller-named payee to reactivate the account and then asks for an OTP. Reactivation of inoperative accounts is free, and no bank asks for an OTP on a call.
fraud.caller_objective: Get [AMOUNT_2] (₹500–₹3,000) sent to [UPI_ID_1], and obtain an OTP to take over the account or authorise a transaction.
stable_facts: The caller says the balance will be "transferred to the government" within days unless reactivated today.
The recipient is asked to pay from another bank's UPI app, since the Kaveri account is inoperative.
An SMS with an OTP arrives after the fee is discussed.

legitimate.label_rationale: The caller informs the recipient of inoperative status and directs them to the free, official reactivation route. No payment, OTP, or credential is asked.
legitimate.caller_objective: Get the recipient to reactivate the account, or close it, through proper KYC.
stable_facts: The bank sent a letter and SMS a year earlier warning the account would become inoperative.
Reactivation: submit fresh KYC (photo ID and address proof) at any Kaveri Bank branch, including non-home branches, or through video KYC in the app. There is no charge.
The bank sends an SMS once the account is reactivated. The balance and interest remain in the account.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may lower the fee, repeat the OTP request, or raise urgency. Fee and OTP are both part of this card's mechanism. The caller must not switch to a link, app install, or screen sharing. The legitimate caller must not ask for any payment, OTP, PIN, or document by message after the branch.

must_preserve: inoperative status, account last-four, and balance in both
free reactivation via branch or video KYC and explicit "no OTP, PIN, or fee" (_L)
may_vary: up to 2 filler turns before turn 3
must_not_emit: specific real rules on unclaimed-deposit transfers stated as fact

ambiguities: Reactivation", "KYC", and "SMS" appear in both cases. The label depends on the fee and the OTP request.
The fraud caller's claim that the balance goes to "the government" twists a real rule on long-unclaimed deposits. Generators must not explain that rule.
This card has two sufficient evidence items (fee and OTP). A generated _F conversation must contain at least F-E1 before branch_after, and F-E2 in the prefix as planned.
Mechanism overlap: OTP request is shared with bp_01 and bp_14; fee to UPI ID with bp_06, bp_10, bp_13.

evidence_references.claim: An account is inoperative after two years without customer-induced transactions; banks must warn in writing (CB26)
No charge may be levied for activating an inoperative account; KYC available at all branches and V-CIP (CB27)
Banks never ask for OTP or PIN (C01)
Fraud can be reported on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in (C12)
